title: About “Pin”
synopsis: You might be familiar with the character 拼 from the word “pinyin”. Here we learn another meaning of the character which can be used to describe a phenomenon in Chinese society.

fullText.simplified:
说“拼”

    “拼”有两个意思。
    第一个意思是“合在一起”，像我们学习中文时首先要学习的“拼音”里的“拼”就是这个意思。经常用的还有“拼车”、“拼饭”、“拼购”，意思是“为了节约钱，几个人合在一起坐车、吃饭或者买东西”。
    第二个意思是“不顾一切地干，比拼”。 在竞争激烈的现代社会，中国人觉得“爱拼才会赢”，这里的“拼”就是这个意思。现在更有“拼爹”这样的词，“拼爹”就是“比拼老爹”。现在有的年轻人上学、找工作、买房子等比拼的不是自己的能力，而是爸爸是否有钱有权。有的人讽刺道：“学好数理化，不如有个好爸爸。”说的就是你即使学习学得再好，再有能力，找的工作等可能也比不上那些有权有钱的爸爸们帮自己儿子找的工作。“拼爹”是中国现代社会一个很不好的现象。
    简单的一个“拼”字反映出中国现代社会的各种现象。你学到了吗？
fullText.traditional:
說“拼”

    “拼”有兩個意思。
    第一個意思是“合在一起”，像我們學習中文時首先要學習的“拼音”裡的“拼”就是這個意思。經常用的還有“拼車”、“拼飯”、“拼購”，意思是“為了節約錢，幾個人合在一起坐車、吃飯或者買東西”。
    第二個意思是“不顧一切地幹，比拼”。 在競爭激烈的現代社會，中國人覺得“愛拼才會贏”，這裡的“拼”就是這個意思。現在更有“拼爹”這樣的詞，“拼爹”就是“比拼老爹”。現在有的年輕人上學、找工作、買房子等比拼的不是自己的能力，而是爸爸是否有錢有權。有的人諷刺道：“學好數理化，不如有個好爸爸。”說的就是你即使學習學得再好，再有能力，找的工作等可能也比不上那些有權有錢的爸爸們幫自己兒子找的工作。“拼爹”是中國現代社會一個很不好的現象。
    簡單的一個“拼”字反映出中國現代社會的各種現象。你學到了嗎？

raw.synopsis: You might be familiar with the character 拼 from the word “pinyin”. Here we learn another meaning of the character which can be used to describe a phenomenon in Chinese society.
sentence_translations: The first meaning is “put together”, just like the meaning of pin in “pinyin” which we learn when we first study Chinese.
Other common usages are the words “carpooling”, “group food ordering” and “group buying”.
Here it means that several people group together to ride a car, eat food or buy things in order to save money.
The second meaning is “to do something recklessly, to compete fiercely”
In today's highly competitive society, Chinese people believe that “you can only win if you love competing fiercely”.
This is the meaning of “pin” here.
Nowadays we also have the word “pin die”, which means “competing through your dad”.
Now when a lot of young people go to school, look for a job, or buy an apartment, ..
.. it is often not their own ability that they compete with, but whether or not their fathers have money and power.
Some say mockingly: “You can learn maths, physics and chemistry, but still lose to someone who has a better dad.”
What it means is that no matter how hard you study, or how talented you are, ..
.. when it comes to finding a job, you still can't compare to those with powerful fathers who help their sons find a job.
“Pin die” is a bad phenomenon in contemporary Chinese society.
A simple “pin” character can reflect many different phenomena in the modern Chinese society.
